title: Christ in the Old Testament
subtitle: How the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms speak of Jesus, sorted into direct references, types and shadows
summary: "Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself" (Luke 24:27). This study follows that reading. A direct reference is a passage that speaks of the Messiah and that the New Testament cites as fulfilled in Jesus. A type is a person or event God shaped to prefigure Him. A shadow is an institution of the Law whose substance is Christ. The categories are a reading aid, not a verdict; many passages carry more than one.

categories.title: Direct reference
categories.note: The passage speaks of the Messiah, and the New Testament cites it as fulfilled in Jesus.

categories.title: Type
categories.note: A person or event God shaped to prefigure Christ, read that way by the New Testament.

categories.title: Shadow
categories.note: An institution or practice of the Law whose substance is Christ (Colossians 2:17, Hebrews 10:1).

categories.title: Witness
categories.note: Jesus and the apostles saying, in so many words, that the Scriptures are about Him.

views.title: By theme
views.note: Nine strands of one witness, from the first promise to the empty tomb and the throne.
